title: Lifecycle growth experiments sprint — kickoff (emails + console nudges + retargeting)
topics: Sprint goals: activation + early retention for self-serve/PLG devs
Onboarding email sequence v1: triggers, cadence, suppression
In-console nudges v1: checklist + banners, feature flags, instrumentation
Retargeting audiences + developer-first messaging + landing page variant
Experiment framework: randomization, holdouts, decision thresholds
Guardrails: deliverability/unsubscribes, support volume, console performance/SLOs
summary: Kickoff for the lifecycle growth experiments sprint. Team aligned on three parallel levers (email sequence, console nudges, retargeting) with shared measurement (activation within 24h/72h, time-to-first-success, D7/D14 retention). Open items: finalize primary activation event definition, confirm event properties + UTM stitching, and lock v1 copy/creative and console nudge scope behind a feature flag with rollback. Guardrails and escalation paths reviewed (deliverability, support tickets, and console SLO impact).

Marissa Cole + Kenji Nakamura: lock console nudge v1 scope (checklist steps + 2 banners) and list exact trigger rules + hide rules
Tessa Morgan + Alicia Perez: deliver final copy + design states for checklist/banners (including edge cases for already-activated users)
Sean Gallagher: confirm guardrail dashboard/alerts and SLO check process for console changes (baseline + post-launch monitoring)

transcript:
Fireflies.ai Transcript

Title: Lifecycle growth experiments sprint — kickoff (emails + console nudges + retargeting)
Date: 2025-01-14
Time: 9:00 AM–9:47 AM PT
Duration: 47 min

Attendees:
- Ben Carter (Growth Marketing)
- Tyler Benson (Marketing Ops / Attribution)
- Marissa Cole (Product, Console)
- Paula Mendes (Telemetry / Experiment requirements)
- Henry Cho (PM, activation milestone)
- Tessa Morgan (Design lead)
- Kenji Nakamura (Nudge UX)
- Alicia Perez (Dashboard/banner design)
- Soojin Lee (Product Marketing)
- Sean Gallagher (SLO / Guardrails)


[00:00] Ben Carter: Cool, alright. I think we’re all on. Um, thanks everyone. This is the kickoff for the lifecycle growth experiments sprint. The goal is pretty simple: lift activation and then early retention for self-serve devs.

[00:17] Ben Carter: Activation, in our words, is like “first successful production-like inference call,” but we have to nail down what that means in events. Henry and Paula, we’ll get to that. The sprint is three levers in parallel: onboarding email sequence, in-console nudges, and retargeting for non-activated and recently lapsed.

[00:39] Marissa Cole: Ben, quick check—when you say “production-like,” are we actually requiring streaming? Or just a 200 response from, like, chat completions.

[00:47] Ben Carter: Exactly the debate. We need a definition that’s measurable and doesn’t overfit. Let’s use this meeting to align on the v1 and the instrumentation plan.

[00:58] Tyler Benson: And from my side, whatever we pick, we need to be able to join campaign touch points to it. So UTMs and event properties have to be consistent, otherwise, it’s gonna be a mess.

[01:09] Soojin Lee: Also please—on messaging—if we’re going to push streaming as “the moment,” we need to be careful we’re not implying it’s required to use Redwood. We can say “recommended for best latency,” but not “you must.”

[01:23] Ben Carter: Yep. Okay. I’ll run an agenda real quick.

[01:28] Ben Carter: Agenda: 1) success metrics and guardrails, 2) experiments list and owners, 3) launch checklist and timeline (Week 0 setup, Week 1 launch, Week 2 iteration, Week 3 readout), and 4) open questions / risks.

[01:43] Ben Carter: Success metrics: activation rate within 24 and 72 hours, time-to-first-success, D7/D14 retention. Then “higher intent” milestones: add billing, increase token usage, create a deployment/route, invite teammates.

[02:02] Sean Gallagher: And guardrails, we’re checking unsubscribe spikes, deliverability, support ticket volume, and also console performance. Like, if a banner adds latency or we make extra network calls on dashboard load, that’s a no.

[02:16] Marissa Cole: Yeah. We have a performance budget for console pages. The checklist component shouldn’t block anything. It has to be async and behind a flag.

[02:25] Kenji Nakamura: For the checklist, the design can be mostly static, and the completion states are based on events we already track—or will track. But we need to know which events are reliable.

[02:38] Paula Mendes: That’s the key. The taxonomy is close, but we’ve had gaps. Like, “first_request_success” is sometimes missing the SDK info. Also we had a mismatch between server-side and client-side names.

[02:52] Tyler Benson: Can we please not have “firstRequestSuccess” in one place and “first_request_success” in another.

[02:56] Paula Mendes: (laughs) Yes, I agree.

[03:00] Ben Carter: Great. Let’s jump into the experiments. Email sequence v1: welcome, quickstart, first success, troubleshooting, and “next step.” We’re targeting new signups who haven’t activated, and we suppress anyone who unsubscribes or is sales-assisted.

[03:18] Tyler Benson: Also suppress existing customers and anyone with “billing_added” already. And we need throttle limits. We’ve seen Gmail clamp down if we spike volume.

[03:28] Ben Carter: Yep. Tyler’s got the deliverability checklist. The email CTA should drive to quickstart docs and/or straight into the console project setup.

[03:38] Alicia Perez: Copy note—if CTA goes into console, we should land them in the right place. Support flagged last quarter we had a routing change and folks hit a 404.

[03:47] Marissa Cole: We can generate a stable link for the onboarding route. But we need a single canonical path and not have Marketing link to, like, three different internal pages.

[03:57] Soojin Lee: And from PMM side: we want consistent promises. A lot of these developers are comparing us to OpenAI or Anthropic, and they expect “copy-paste and it works.” So email tone has to be dev-first, not fluffy.

[04:14] Ben Carter: Okay. Second lever: console nudges. Marissa, Kenji, can you describe v1 scope.

[04:20] Marissa Cole: V1 is a setup checklist on the dashboard and two contextual banners. Checklist steps are something like: create API key, make first request, try streaming, view latency/cost dashboard. Banners: one if you created a key but haven’t made a request in 2 hours; another after repeated auth errors.

[04:44] Kenji Nakamura: Trigger rules: show banner after, like, two 401/403 errors within 10 minutes. Hide after “first_request_success.” And we should have a “dismiss” that respects the user.

[04:55] Paula Mendes: For those errors, we need to ensure the console actually receives error codes reliably. Some errors happen server-side from API calls outside console. So we might only see them if SDK telemetry is present.

[05:10] Marissa Cole: Right, so for the auth error banner, we might scope to console-originated requests only, or we attach it to “api_key_created but no success after X time.”

[05:20] Ben Carter: Makes sense. The idea is “just-in-time” help, not spam.

[05:26] Tessa Morgan: UX note: We should avoid a wall of nags. Checklist can be collapsible. And the empty states should be calm, like: “Need a hand? Here’s the curl command.” Not like “You haven’t done this!”

[05:43] Alicia Perez: Also accessibility: banners must be keyboard focusable, not trap focus, and have ARIA labels. I’ll put that into the spec.

[05:52] Ben Carter: Third lever: retargeting. Audience is non-activated signups and lapsed users (activated once but no activity in 7–14 days). Messaging is developer-first: latency/cost/reliability with proof points.

[06:08] Soojin Lee: Quick caution: proof points must be substantiated. If we say “2x faster,” we need a public benchmark link or a doc post. Also, we should avoid implying we’re always cheaper than everyone.

[06:20] Ben Carter: Totally. Ethan is helping with benchmark content, but we’ll keep claims modest.

[06:27] Tyler Benson: For retargeting measurement, we’ll use UTMs to a landing page variant. Then we capture UTMs in product events. The join will be last-touch within, say, 7 days. We just need to be explicit that attribution is directional.

[06:44] Paula Mendes: And that data has to respect consent and unsubscribe rules. Marketing tracking review is underway, but keep it minimal. No weird identifiers.

[06:55] Tyler Benson: We’ll use hashed user ID in our system; ad platforms get their own thing. No raw emails exported.

[07:03] Ben Carter: Perfect. Now, main open question: activation definition. Henry, can you walk us through options.

[07:10] Henry Cho: Sure. We have a few candidates.

[07:13] Henry Cho: Option A: “first_request_success” defined as first 2xx completion from any inference endpoint (chat/text/embeddings) with at least, like, N tokens or a minimum payload.

[07:26] Henry Cho: Option B: “first_streaming_success” because it indicates a more real integration—people wired streaming and it worked.

[07:35] Henry Cho: Option C: “dashboard_viewed” after a success, which indicates they’re exploring cost/latency and probably more engaged.

[07:43] Henry Cho: The risk with streaming is it’s a higher bar and could undercount activation for embeddings users. The risk with first 2xx is it might include trivial “hello world” that doesn’t predict retention.

[07:58] Ben Carter: My vote is first 2xx as primary activation, and we track streaming and dashboard as secondary milestones.

[08:06] Marissa Cole: That makes sense for broad coverage. But we should add a property for “endpoint_type” so we can segment chat vs embeddings.

[08:16] Paula Mendes: Yep. Properties we need: sdk_language, endpoint_type, model_id, region, request_tokens-ish (or approximate), and whether it was streaming.

[08:30] Tyler Benson: Please also include utm_source, utm_campaign, utm_medium where available. But we should only populate that if they came from a campaign click, not for every user.

[08:40] Paula Mendes: Right, it’ll be optional properties.

[08:44] Sean Gallagher: Also, careful with “request_tokens.” That might not be known at request time or may change. But for guardrails, we’re not gating anything. Just measurement.

[08:57] Ben Carter: Cool. On decision thresholds: we’re not doing like a full stats thesis here. We’ll use heuristics—if activation lifts meaningfully, and guardrails are green, we roll forward. Sana will help with analysis but the question is “ship, iterate, or roll back.”

[09:17] Tyler Benson: Sample size: for email, we should get enough volume quickly. Console nudges might take longer because it’s behind a flag and we’re only showing to new signups.

[09:28] Marissa Cole: Yep, and we’ll likely do 50/50 split or maybe 70/30 to reduce risk.

[09:34] Paula Mendes: Randomization unit: user_id, sticky assignment. Holdout group exists.

[09:40] Ben Carter: Great. Let’s go to timeline.

[09:45] Ben Carter: Week 0: tracking/copy/UX specs. Week 1: launch v1 across all three levers. Week 2: iterate variants and fix bugs. Week 3: readout.

[09:58] Tessa Morgan: For Week 0 design, we need final checklist step list today or tomorrow, otherwise we’re guessing.

[10:04] Henry Cho: I can share the step list today but it’s dependent on what events are stable.

[10:10] Paula Mendes: I’ll confirm event stability tomorrow. There’s a PR in flight to standardize names.

[10:17] Marissa Cole: Also feature flag and rollback: we need that defined. If guardrails trip, we need to turn it off quickly.

[10:25] Sean Gallagher: We can set alerts. Like if support-link clicks in banners spike, or console errors increase. But we should define thresholds. Unsub rate is marketing side, performance is mine.

[10:41] Ben Carter: Tyler, do you have a proposed unsubscribe threshold.

[10:44] Tyler Benson: For onboarding sequence, if unsub goes above, like, 0.8% on any email, we pause that email. And spam complaint rate if it goes above 0.1%, we stop and investigate.

[10:58] Ben Carter: Great. Support volume.

[11:01] Sean Gallagher: Dev Patel owns support guardrails, but we can use “support contact clicks” as a proxy plus actual ticket tags. We should tag tickets with “lifecycle-sprint” if it’s related.

[11:14] Marissa Cole: We can add a “contact support” link parameter from banner that tags it.

[11:19] Alicia Perez: I’ll make sure the support link has the right tracking and that the copy doesn’t sound like “you’re stuck,” more like “Need help?”

[11:29] Ben Carter: Okay. Now, owners recap. Email: Ben + Tyler + Soojin for copy approval. Console nudges: Marissa + Kenji + Alicia + Tessa. Instrumentation: Paula + Logan (not on today) + Eng. Retargeting: Ben + Soojin + Tyler.

[11:51] Soojin Lee: Can we align on the core messaging pillars we’re using across all surfaces? Like, no matter if it’s email, banner, or ad.

[11:59] Ben Carter: Yes. The pillars are: predictable latency, cost controls (batching/caching/quant), and reliability with fallbacks. But we won’t go deep on quantization in ads.

[12:11] Soojin Lee: Exactly. Keep it simple: “fast, reliable inference” and “see token-level cost/latency in the console.”

[12:19] Kenji Nakamura: For the checklist, “View your cost and latency” is a good step. It nudges them to the dashboard which is sticky.

[12:28] Marissa Cole: We should ensure the dashboard loads for brand new accounts though. There’s sometimes a blank state if no data.

[12:35] Alicia Perez: I can design the empty state: “No requests yet—run your first request to populate latency and cost.”

[12:45] Paula Mendes: And instrumentation: dashboard_viewed should fire even if it’s empty state, so we know they looked.

[12:54] Tyler Benson: But as secondary metric, not the primary activation.

[12:57] Ben Carter: Right.

[13:01] (crosstalk)

[13:02] Ben Carter: Okay. Risks. One: link routing or broken CTAs. Two: event instrumentation missing fields. Three: over-emailing causing deliverability issues. Four: banners hurting console performance or annoying users.

[13:20] Sean Gallagher: On performance, the safe path is: no extra API calls in render. Use cached user state. If we must call, do it after load.

[13:29] Marissa Cole: Agreed.

[13:31] Tessa Morgan: On “annoying,” we should keep the nudges contextual and let users dismiss. If they dismiss, we respect it for like a week.

[13:41] Kenji Nakamura: Yeah, “snooze” maybe.

[13:44] Ben Carter: Great. For troubleshooting email, we need to address top blockers. Aparna and Support have been sharing: auth errors, streaming disconnects, and model selection confusion.

[13:58] Soojin Lee: We should also add a line that says “If you’re embedding-heavy, here’s the embeddings quickstart.” Not everyone is doing chat.

[14:07] Ben Carter: Good call.

[14:10] Tyler Benson: Also, segmentation: if the first request is embeddings, then we send different “next step” email—like rerankers or a route.

[14:20] Ben Carter: Not in v1, but maybe in v2. Let’s not overbuild.

[14:26] Henry Cho: For the experiment tracker, we need each experiment ID, start/stop, primary metric, guardrails, and status.

[14:34] Ben Carter: Yep, I’ll update the tracker today.

[14:38] Paula Mendes: Also data quality gaps. If we don’t have sdk_language reliably, we can’t slice by SDK. But that’s a key cut.

[14:47] Marissa Cole: For console, we can capture it for in-console requests, but not for API calls from their app unless they use our SDK.

[14:56] Paula Mendes: We can infer from user agent for some, but it’s not perfect.

[15:02] Ben Carter: Okay. It’s fine. We’ll do best effort.

[15:06] Tyler Benson: For email, we can at least know which quickstart links they clicked by language.

[15:12] Ben Carter: Great.

[15:14] Ben Carter: Let’s do a quick go/no-go criteria for Week 1 launch. For emails, deliverability checks green. For console nudges, feature flag and rollback tested. For retargeting, audiences and pixel/UTM capture validated.

[15:30] Sean Gallagher: And for console, we do a quick SLO smoke test in staging and then monitor error rate post-launch.

[15:37] Marissa Cole: Yep. We’ll do that.

[15:40] Ben Carter: We’re at time. Last round: anything blocking.

[15:45] Tessa Morgan: Just need final checklist steps and copy constraints.

[15:49] Soojin Lee: I’ll send the “do/don’t” for claims and tone today.

[15:54] Tyler Benson: I’ll publish UTM conventions and suppression rules. Also, note: we had a suppression bug previously—so we need QA on opt-out.

[16:04] Paula Mendes: I’ll coordinate with Eng on event schema validation.

[16:08] Marissa Cole: I’ll confirm feature flag owners and rollback process.

[16:12] Ben Carter: Perfect. I’ll send notes and update the tracker. Thanks everyone.

[16:18] (meeting ends shortly after; minor post-call chatter)
